stories.headline: Hegseth taps Musk, Luckey and Gingrich to lead Pentagon's 120-day 'Project Meridian' warfare study

key_facts.fact: On September 30, 2026, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that Elon Musk, Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich will lead 'Project Meridian', a new Pentagon effort to study the future of warfare.
key_facts.excerpt: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced that xAI CEO Elon Musk, Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey and former Speaker Newt Gingrich(R-Ga.) will lead a new Pentagon effort to study the future of warfare, dubbed "Project Meridian."

key_facts.fact: The trio works under Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael; Hegseth said the project is 'futuristic on purpose' and is not meant to develop new strategies or policies.
key_facts.excerpt: "It is futuristic on purpose," he said of the project, which he said was not meant to develop new strategies or policies.

key_facts.fact: A September 30 memo gives Project Meridian until January 28, 2027 (120 days) to identify the weapons and technologies warfighters will need and propose ways to develop, test and field them, citing AI, autonomy, directed energy, robotics and biotechnology.
key_facts.excerpt: propose actionable solutions to start developing, testing and fielding these capabilities" no later than Jan. 28, 2027, or 120 days from now.

key_facts.fact: The findings will be released as a public unclassified report with a classified annex, covering domains 'from subterranean depths to the cislunar frontier'.
key_facts.excerpt: The department says they will come as an unclassified report released to the public, with a classified annex. The project will cover every future warfighting domain, "from subterranean depths to the cislunar frontier"

key_facts.fact: Meridian was one of six initiatives Hegseth unveiled, alongside an Autonomous Warfare Command the department wants running as a four-star combatant command by October 1, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Meridian was one of six initiatives Hegseth unveiled. Another is the Autonomous Warfare Command. The department wants it running as a four-star functional combatant command by 1 October 2027.

key_facts.fact: The role marks Musk's first return to government work since he ran the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge).
key_facts.excerpt: marking the SpaceX CEO's first return to government since he ran the chaotic, so-called "department of government efficiency", or Doge.

key_facts.fact: Fox News noted the appointments could raise conflict-of-interest questions, since Musk's SpaceX and Luckey's Anduril compete for defense business.
key_facts.excerpt: It could also raise potential conflict-of-interest questions as executives whose companies compete for defense business help identify the capabilities and technologies the military should pursue.

stories.headline: Iran's cabinet reviews US response to Hormuz plan as mediators draft deal and rial hits record low

key_facts.fact: On September 30, Iranian officials said they had received an official US response to Tehran's latest proposal to end the seven-month war; Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented it to President Masoud Pezeshkian at a cabinet meeting, without disclosing its content.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the U.S. response to President Masoud Pezeshkian at a Cabinet meeting, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani told the state-run IRNA news agency.

key_facts.fact: Pezeshkian said Iran 'will make every effort to bring the agreement to fruition' and that it must be based on a 'win-win strategy'.
key_facts.excerpt: "We will make every effort to bring the agreement to fruition and will firmly stand up for the rights of the Iranian people," Pezeshkian said. "The agreement must now be based on a win-win strategy."

key_facts.fact: Officials told AP that mediators are working on a draft that would first reopen the Strait of Hormuz with no tolls and lift the US blockade of Iranian ports, then remove sanctions; the US says no deal until nuclear issues are addressed.
key_facts.excerpt: mediators are working with both sides on a proposal that would include reopening the strait and lifting the U.S. blockade, and then removing sanctions... it would include no tolls

key_facts.fact: Iran's rial fell to a new record low of more than 2.5 million to the US dollar, 27 days after the previous low of 2.2 million on September 2.
key_facts.excerpt: traders in Tehran exchanging more than 2.5 million rials to the U.S. dollar... The latest decline came just 27 days after the rial hit its previous record low of 2.2 million to the dollar on Sept. 2.

key_facts.fact: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said unknown projectiles struck three ships in the strait on Tuesday, including a crude oil tanker, while an IRGC spokesman said Iranian forces keep hitting small ships.
key_facts.excerpt: the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre said unknown projectiles struck three ships in the waterway on Tuesday, including a crude oil tanker.

key_facts.fact: Kpler data show Middle East crude exports reached about 16.3 million barrels per day in September, the highest since the war began and just under 80% of pre-war levels, weakening Iran's leverage.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude exports reached an estimated 16.328 million barrels per day (bpd) in September – their highest level since the war began... Middle East crude exports have recovered to just less than 80 percent of their pre-war level.

stories.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hits 19-year high of 5.30% despite softer inflation; Dow falls 0.86%

key_facts.fact: On September 30, the 10-year Treasury yield rose to a 19-year high of 5.304% intraday, settling at 5.293%, as stronger US data and rising crude pushed bonds lower.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year T-note yield rose +5.7 bp to 5.293%. Dec T-notes tumbled to a 19-year nearest-futures low on Wednesday, and the 10-year T-note yield rose to a 19-year high of 5.304%.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 closed down 0.25%, the Dow Jones fell 0.86% to a 3.5-month low, and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.23%.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 Index ($SPX) (SPY) closed down by -0.25% on Wednesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DOWI) (DIA) closed down by -0.86%, and the Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) (QQQ) closed up +0.23%... the Dow Jones Industrial falling to a 3.5-month low.

key_facts.fact: Bonds sold off on stronger-than-expected Q2 GDP, September ADP employment and the Chicago PMI, and WTI crude rose more than 1% after Russia extended its ban on most diesel exports through October.
key_facts.excerpt: T-notes gave up an early advance on Wednesday and turned lower on stronger-than-expected US economic news, including Q2 GDP, the Sep ADP employment change, and the Sep MNI Chicago PMI... after Russia announced that it was extending a ban on most diesel exports through October

key_facts.fact: Softer-than-expected core PCE data cut the market-implied chance of a Fed rate hike in October to 35% from 52% on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: The better-than-expected inflation news reduced the chance of a Fed rate hike next month to 35% from 52% on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Reuters said long-dated US Treasury yields rose for the seventh straight day; for the quarter, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained while the Dow ended lower.
key_facts.excerpt: long-dated US Treasury yields moved higher for the seventh straight day... For the quarter, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq posted gains, but the Dow ended the July-September period lower.

key_facts.fact: In September, the Dow fell 4.3% and the S&P 500 0.5%, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: the Nasdaq Composite finished September up 1.9%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.5%, the DJIA fell 4.3%, the Russell 2000 fell 5.3%

stories.headline: FDA extends BMS's Camzyos to children with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

key_facts.fact: Bristol Myers Squibb announced on September 30 that the FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) in adults and pediatric patients weighing 30 kg (66 lb) or more.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved CAMZYOS ® (mavacamten) for the treatment of symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) to improve functional capacity and symptoms in adults and pediatric patients weighing 30 kg (66 lbs) or more.

key_facts.fact: Camzyos becomes the only FDA-approved oHCM therapy for children and adolescents, and BMS says it now has the broadest indication of any cardiac myosin inhibitor.
key_facts.excerpt: making it the only FDA-approved therapy for oHCM in a pediatric population

key_facts.fact: The approval is based on the phase 3 SCOUT-HCM trial.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is based on findings from the phase 3 SCOUT-HCM trial.

key_facts.fact: Camzyos was first approved in 2022 for adults and has been prescribed by more than 5,000 US providers to over 25,000 patients; BMS is discussing pediatric data with other regulators.
key_facts.excerpt: CAMZYOS has been prescribed by more than 5,000 healthcare providers (HCPs) to over 25,000 patients in the U.S. alone. Beyond this U.S. approval, the pediatric data is being discussed with multiple global regulatory authorities

stories.headline: Rocket Lab signs largest-ever Electron deal: 20 launches for Japan's Synspective

key_facts.fact: On September 30, Rocket Lab announced a multi-year agreement for 20 new Electron launches with Tokyo-based Earth observation company Synspective, its largest commercial Electron contract ever.
key_facts.excerpt: today announced it has signed a multi-year launch agreement for 20 new Electron missions with Tokyo-based Earth observation company Synspective. The contract is the largest commercial launch contract for Electron in Rocket Lab's history

key_facts.fact: The missions will put StriX synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites into sun-synchronous orbit from 2028 through 2031; financial terms were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab will launch 20 StriX synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites to sun-synchronous orbit (SSO) from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1. The missions are scheduled to take place annually from 2028 through 2031

key_facts.fact: Synspective now has 47 Electron launches contracted, 34 not yet flown, the most of any Rocket Lab customer; 13 StriX satellites have launched so far.
key_facts.excerpt: This agreement brings Synspective's total contracted launches with Rocket Lab to 47, 34 of which have yet to fly... has successfully launched 13 StriX SAR satellites to date.

key_facts.fact: Rocket Lab's launch backlog has passed 100 missions after a series of multi-launch contracts this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's launch backlog has now surpassed 100 missions following a series of multi-launch contracts this year

stories.headline: Grindr agrees to buy HIV-prevention telehealth firm Freddie's parent PurposeMed for $250M

key_facts.fact: On September 30, Grindr agreed to acquire PurposeMed, parent of PrEP and HIV-prevention telehealth provider Freddie, for $250 million: $190 million in cash and $60 million in Grindr stock.
key_facts.excerpt: Grindr will acquire PurposeMed Inc. (inclusive of the Freddie brand and its partnerships with affiliated clinical networks) for $250 million, consisting of $190 million in cash and $60 million in Grindr common stock.

key_facts.fact: The deal includes up to $70 million more in cash tied to 2027 performance targets, payable in 2028, and is expected to close in Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement also includes the potential for up to $70 million in additional cash consideration tied to 2027 performance targets, payable in 2028... expected to close in Q4 2026

key_facts.fact: Freddie, founded in Canada in 2020, serves more than 25,000 active patients and expects 2026 revenue above $80 million with over $10 million in adjusted EBITDA.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the end of September, the business serves over 25,000 active patients. Freddie expects to generate 2026 revenue of more than $80 million and more than $10 million in Adjusted EBITDA.

key_facts.fact: Grindr told shareholders the healthcare business could become as large as, if not larger than, its core dating business; the US model generates over $400 in monthly revenue per active patient.
key_facts.excerpt: we are catalyzing a healthcare business that we believe can be as large as, if not larger than, the core Grindr business is today... The combined US telehealth and pharmacy model generates more than $400 in monthly revenue per active patient

key_facts.fact: Freddie expanded into the US in 2024, now serves all 50 states and DC, and the deal builds on Grindr's Woodwork telehealth service launched in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Freddie, founded in Canada in 2020, expanded into the United States in 2024 and now serves patients in all 50 states and Washington, D.C.

stories.headline: Visa-, Mastercard- and Stripe-backed OUSD stablecoin goes live with $1B+ in launch liquidity

key_facts.fact: Open USD (OUSD), a dollar stablecoin from Open Standard, went live on September 30 on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo; it was first unveiled in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Open USD (OUSD), after being initially unveiled in June, went live on Wednesday on Ethereum, Solana, Coinbase's Base and Stripe-backed Tempo blockchains

key_facts.fact: Founding partners Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa each hold an equal initial equity stake and together committed more than $1 billion to seed OUSD liquidity.
key_facts.excerpt: developed by Open Standard with founding partners Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa. The founding five committed over $1 billion to seed initial liquidity, and each received an equal initial equity stake.

key_facts.fact: OUSD is issued by Stripe-owned Bridge, with reserves held at BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY and monthly attestations promised; businesses can mint and redeem 1:1 via BVNK, Stripe and the Visa Stablecoin Platform.
key_facts.excerpt: OUSD is issued by Bridge and runs natively on Base, Ethereum, Solana, and Tempo. Reserves are held at BlackRock, Lead Bank, and BNY, with monthly attestations promised.

key_facts.fact: Stripe made OUSD its default stablecoin across its products, while saying users will not be required to convert existing stablecoin balances.
key_facts.excerpt: OUSD on Tempo is now Stripe's default stablecoin configuration... won't require Stripe users to convert their existing stablecoin balances to OUSD.

key_facts.fact: The partner roster grew from more than 140 companies at the June unveiling to over 200; Coinbase access begins October 1, and the token trades first on Coinbase, Kraken and Uniswap.
key_facts.excerpt: It trades on Coinbase, Kraken and Uniswap at launch. Businesses can mint and redeem OUSD at a 1:1 rate against the dollar at no cost through BVNK (owned by Mastercard), Stripe and the Visa Stablecoin Platform starting today, with Coinbase access beginning Oct. 1.

key_facts.fact: The launch positions OUSD against the dominant stablecoins USDT (Tether) and USDC (Circle), with a model that spreads economics across distributing partners.
key_facts.excerpt: targets payments, banking, settlement and institutional trading in a stablecoin market still dominated by USDT and USDC.
